name: Mod and mini
summary: The young London look of the 1960s: the miniskirt, the short shift, a slim jacket and a bold print, sold by small boutiques.

philosophy.core_thesis: Fashion belongs to the young and the street: a short hem, a clean cut and a bold print show speed and fun.
design_principles: Raise the hem to 10 to 20 cm above the knee for a miniskirt.
Cut the dress as a short, straight shift or an A-line, with the waist seam low or gone.
Keep the line clean: no darts that show, no ruffle, no trim.
Use bold shapes and op-art prints in black and white, or flat bright colours.
Use tights in opaque wool or nylon, and a flat or low-heeled shoe.
Cut the mod suit slim, with a short jacket, narrow lapels and a narrow trouser.
Make the fashion in small runs, and sell it in a boutique that opens late and plays music.
anti_patterns: A built waist and a full petticoat skirt
A fussy trim of lace and bows

silhouette.shape: A short, straight or A-line shift, a miniskirt above the knee and a slim jacket.
silhouette.line: A high hem, a low or absent waist, a round neckline, a small collar and a bare arm.
silhouette.fit: Close and light on the body; the dress hangs from the shoulder and does not hold the waist.
silhouette.proportion: Hem 10 to 20 cm above the knee on the miniskirt; jacket ends at the hip bone; trouser leg about 40 cm at the hem.
rules: Raise the hem above the knee and keep the cut straight.
Use a clean seam, a round collar and a zip in place of buttons or bows.
Print the cloth in a large, flat, high-contrast pattern.
Add white tights or opaque tights, and a flat or low-heeled shoe.
Cut a man's jacket short, with two buttons and a narrow lapel.

fabrics.rule: Choose a light, clean cloth that holds a short, straight line: wool crêpe and jersey for the dress, gabardine for the coat, PVC for rain.

methods: short, straight pattern with few seams
slim suit cut on a short block
construction.closures: A back zip, a large metal ring, a snap or a plain button.
construction.details: A round or Peter Pan collar, a short sleeve or none, a cut-out, a flat bow, a patent shoe and large round earrings.

surface.pattern: Op-art black and white, large flat flowers, stripes and checks; plain bright colour blocks.
surface.gloss: Wool and jersey at 3–8 GU; PVC at 60–90 GU.
surface.wear: The style wants a new, bright and fresh piece; it is cheap, made in a short run, and worn for a season.

palette.strategy: Strong black and white, and flat, bright primary colours.

processes: boutique design for the young customer
making.scale: Boutique and small factory: short runs, a new line each season, and cheap copies in the high street; the young buyer set the price.
making.signs: A high hem, a clean flat cut, a bold flat colour or print, and a zip in place of a button.

pieces.form: A-line shift dress with an op-art print
Slim, short mod jacket with narrow lapels
Raincoat of shiny PVC with a high collar
Poplin blouse with a Peter Pan collar

evidence.title: King's Road, London UK - Mary Quant boutique location.jpg

emotion.target_response: A sense of speed and fun: the viewer sees a short hem and a bold print and reads youth, noise and freedom.

use_cases: a period costume brief for a 1960s film in London
a retro mini dress or a mod suit line
a fashion image prompt for Carnaby Street in 1966
a study note on the youthquake
avoid_when: the brief is formal or a ball gown
the brief is a long skirt
the brief wants a built waist and a full skirt

modifiers.how: Use white and silver, PVC and a geometric cut, and add a helmet or a visor.
Drop the hem to the ankle, use soft cotton with flowers, and loosen the cut.

ornament_level.note: The cut is plain; colour and print carry the style.
